Write the mean function as $\truemean$, not as $f$.
The mean function is the population mean of the outcome given the inputs, $\truemeanf{x}$.
In a group that uses shared macros (see [Using shared macros](#using-shared-macros)),
write it `\truemeanf{x}`.

Name the object you mean.
When the text refers to the fitted prediction function as a concept,
the rule that turns an input into a predicted outcome,
write the fitted prediction function, not the fitted mean function.
Write it `\epredfnf{x}` (symbol $\epredfn$) for an estimated one, or `\predfnf{x}` (symbol $\predfn$) for any prediction function.
Use the fitted or estimated mean function only where the text is about
estimating the mean function $\truemean$ itself.

::: {#exm-mean-vs-prediction-function}

## Mean function and fitted prediction function

> ❌ The expected squared error of the fitted mean function at $x$ is $\E{(y - \hat{f}(x))^2}$.
>
> ✅ The expected squared error of the fitted prediction function at $x$ is $\E{\paren{\outvar - \epredfnf{x}}^2}$,
> and its bias is $\E{\epredfnf{x}} - \truemeanf{x}$.

The ✅ version names the fitted prediction function where the concept is a prediction,
and keeps $\truemean$ for the mean it is compared with.

:::
